status: SUPERSEDED -- kept as the record of a run whose comparison was not clean

physics_informed_comparison.optimizer: Adam lr=2e-3 wd=0.0, x0.9 every 1000 epochs

why_superseded: the two runs did not share an optimizer. The physics-informed model uses plain Adam at lr=2e-3 with weight_decay=0 and a x0.9-every-1000-epochs decay; this run used AdamW at lr=1e-3 with weight_decay=1e-5 and OneCycleLR, which is very likely the better recipe. The 0.0826-vs-0.0959 gap therefore cannot be attributed to the training principle: the optimizer is confounded with the loss. train_data_driven.py now matches the physics-informed optimizer by default and the run must be repeated.
still_valid: the label-generation cost, 5.65 h of CPU for 800 B1 x Neo-Hookean solves at Table 4a's measured rate, which the physics-informed model does not pay. That figure does not depend on the optimizer.
also_worth_noting: the best step was 75,000 of 75,000 -- the last one. The run had not converged when the step budget ran out, so its number is a lower bound on what this recipe reaches, not its ceiling.
